- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.50), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 7 days.  
- If 3+ consecutive days of high sentiment (≥0.75) precede forecast, model tends to overreact; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast for next 5 days.  
- If forecast is consistently higher than true outcome over 5+ days, apply downward adjustment: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.25–0.75), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3-day moving average of true values as baseline for next 7 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >2% from 15-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent trend (not just historical mean).
